record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.original_question: Why do technically demanding AC-susceptibility and specific-heat experiments on high-dilution LiHoxY1−xF4 disagree about whether the system shows conventional spin-glass freezing or unusual antiglass behavior, particularly between the earlier measurements of Reich, Ghosh, and collaborators and the later measurements of Quilliam and collaborators?

evidence.quote: Recent measurements by Quilliam et al. [79] contradict the earlier results [74, 75, 76] and find that the frequency distribution of χ”, broadens as the temperature is reduced also in the high dilution limit (x = 4.5%) as shown in the left panel of Fig. 2.

Furthermore, the specific heat data reported in Ref. [80] do not display any of the unusual features that were previously interpreted as a telltale signature of entangled magnetic moments within a quantum disordered antiglass state [77].

The reason for the difference between the AC susceptibility and specific heat experimental results of Refs. [74, 75, 76, 77] and Refs. [79, 80] remains an open question. Due to the very slow dynamics, all these measurements are technically very demanding.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the dilute dipolar-coupled Ising magnet LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ in the high-dilution regime (e.g. $x \approx 0.045$), where Ho$^{3+}$ ions occupy a small fraction of the rare-earth sites and interact predominantly through long-ranged magnetic dipolar interactions with a small transverse off-diagonal exchange that introduces effective quantum fluctuations. The low-temperature, low-frequency magnetic response of this system has been probed by AC magnetic susceptibility (real and imaginary parts $\chi'(\omega,T)$ and $\chi''(\omega,T)$) and by specific heat $C(T)$ measurements down to millikelvin temperatures.

One set of careful experiments reports: (a) a quasi-static susceptibility $\chi_0(T)$ that diverges with an anomalous power law $\chi_0 \sim T^{-0.75}$, (b) a frequency distribution of $\chi''$ that narrows as the temperature is lowered, and (c) specific-heat features interpreted as signatures of a quantum-disordered "antiglass" state with entangled magnetic moments rather than a conventional spin glass. Another set of equally careful experiments on nominally identical samples reports: (a$'$) no such anomalous divergence of $\chi_0$, (b$'$) a frequency distribution of $\chi''$ that broadens upon cooling (as expected for canonical spin-glass freezing), and (c$'$) a specific heat lacking the unusual features attributed to the antiglass phase.

Problem. Identify and justify a quantitative physical mechanism — taking into account ingredients such as nuclear hyperfine couplings to the Ho$^{3+}$ electronic moments, off-diagonal dipolar terms generating an effective random transverse field, sample-dependent demagnetization and shape effects, thermal contact and equilibration on extremely long relaxation timescales, and possible non-equilibrium / aging dynamics — that explains the discrepancy between the two sets of AC-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements on highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$, and determine which (if either) of the two scenarios (conventional spin-glass freezing versus antiglass quantum-disordered behavior) describes the true equilibrium low-temperature phase of the system in the high-dilution limit.
artifact.category_tag: dilute dipolar Ising magnets / spin glasses
artifact.status_search_result: The discrepancy between the earlier antiglass-supporting AC-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements (Reich, Ghosh and collaborators) and the later spin-glass-consistent measurements (Quilliam et al.) on highly diluted LiHo$_x$Y$_{1-x}$F$_4$ remains unresolved in the literature. Subsequent works (e.g. μSR studies and perturbative quantum Monte Carlo analyses) have continued to debate the existence of an antiglass phase versus conventional spin-glass freezing without converging on an accepted explanation for the experimental disagreement.

status_evidence.title: Specific Heat of the Dilute Ising Magnet LiHoxY1-xF4 (Quilliam et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Specific heat data on dilute LiHoxY1-xF4 do not show the anomalous features previously interpreted as antiglass behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Specific-heat measurements by Quilliam et al. contradict earlier antiglass interpretations.

status_evidence.title: Evidence of spin glass dynamics in dilute LiHoxY1-xF4
status_evidence.snippet: Frequency and temperature dependences of the susceptibility show characteristic glassy relaxation, with the absorption spectrum broadening with decreasing temperature, suggesting spin-glass rather than exotic spin-liquid behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Later AC susceptibility data favor conventional spin-glass freezing rather than antiglass behavior.

status_evidence.title: μSR study of the anti-glass LiHo0.045Y0.955F4
status_evidence.snippet: μSR investigation of the proposed antiglass state in highly diluted LiHo0.045Y0.955F4.
status_evidence.claim: Independent probes have continued to investigate but not definitively resolve the antiglass-versus-spin-glass question.
